## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Mātikā* ("Matrix") constitutes the opening text (Ps 1.0) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* in the late Khuddaka strata of the Pali Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Functioning as a formal matrix or schedule of doctrinal categories, it sets out the systematic headings and thematic taxonomies that are analyzed in the subsequent treatises of the work, most prominently the opening *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1) [DharmaNexus]. Four modern translations in four languages are cataloged by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse analyses computed by DharmaNexus record 544 matching passages across 19 other Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The text's most substantial alignment is with the following *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1), which elaborates its list of knowledges in detail (223 matches, encompassing nearly 20,000 shared characters, including an extended match between segments §63.1–73.1 and §576.3_1–576.3_5) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares passages with the *Indriyakathā* (Ps 1.4) as well as canonical Abhidhamma texts, specifically the *Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga* (Vb 15), the *Ñāṇavibhaṅga* (Vb 16), and the *Dukanikkhepa* of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (Ds 2.3.2) [DharmaNexus]. In post-canonical literature, the *Mātikā* is heavily cited or paralleled in the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* and Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga*, alongside several other *aṭṭhakathā* and *ṭīkā* works such as the *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā*, *Majjhimanikāya-aṭṭhakathā*, *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā*, and *Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments detected by DharmaNexus reflect shared technical doctrinal vocabulary with Mahāyāna and Sanskrit scholastic texts, including Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya*, Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā*, and Tibetan versions of the *Mahāvyutpatti* (D4346) and *Buddhāvataṃsaka-sūtra* (D0044) [DharmaNexus].
